transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hello, Dr. Smith. I’m scared that if I start eating more, I’ll lose control and put on weight I can’t afford at my age and in my line of work. I've always had to maintain strict discipline, and the idea of gaining weight makes me feel like I'd be losing my grip entirely.

Do you ever feel that you lose control over your eating and consume an unusually large amount of food in a short period, and if so, do you use any methods like vomiting or excessive exercise to compensate?

No, it's actually the exact opposite—I don't binge or purge at all. I strictly limit myself to just a black coffee in the morning and maybe a small piece of chicken or an apple late at night because I'm terrified that eating any more than that will make me lose control and gain weight.

When you look in the mirror, do you see your body shape or weight differently than how others describe you, or do you feel that your self-worth is almost entirely determined by your ability to keep your weight low?

When I look in the mirror, I don't see a skinny guy; I just see a gut and flabby arms that make me feel like a failure as a cop and as a man. Keeping that number on the scale from going up feels like the only thing I still have any control over right now. My entire self-worth has basically become tied to maintaining that discipline.
